title: The Barricades of Paris
summary: Paris, July 2769. The Free Assembly holds the city behind its barricades and Varenne sits in the Hôtel de Ville. Field Marshal Fairleigh takes it back street by street.

sides.name: The Crown
sides.about: Field Marshal Fairleigh's army, Colonel Ruggieri's guns and the King's chaplain, Father Tomasz.

sides.name: The Free Assembly
sides.about: Varenne's Paris: the barricades of the faubourg, the bridges, the torches and the hall. Green and black.

objectives.text: Take the three barricades of the faubourg: {taken} of 3. Break them with the guns: the Mortar lobs over, the cannon's canister sweeps the street.
Take the bridges to the Cité, the Pont Notre-Dame and the Pont au Change: {bridges} of 2.
Notre-Dame must not burn: stop the torch-bearers coming over the Petit Pont.
Take Varenne ALIVE: open the hall's palisade, wear him down, then a man of yours beside him. Don't let him reach the boats.
Hold Paris: burn Notre-Dame, bring down the Field Marshal, or get Varenne out by the river.

options.label: SPARE HIM: EXILE
options.about: Father Tomasz asks for his life. A ship, and never French ground again.

options.label: EXECUTE HIM
options.about: The King's law for the man who burned Virginia and raised Paris. At dawn, on the Grève.

k_open1.text: Paris rose in the summer of 2769. Not a riot: a city behind its own walls, with a government in its hall.

k_open2.text: Fairleigh took it back. He was a field marshal by then. Let him tell it; he tells it shorter than I do.

f_open1.text: We camped outside the Porte Saint-Antoine. Beyond the gate the faubourg was one long street, and they had cut it three times.

f_open_printer.text: The printer the young Father took at Lyon had named Paris. He was right about that, if about nothing else.

f_open_noprinter.text: We had no word from inside the city. We learnt its streets the hard way.

f_open_saved.text: The Hollins boys came over with the Virginia volunteers. They had asked to.

f_open2.text: Ruggieri had his guns, and the King had sent us something new from the foundries: a mortar, to throw a shell over a wall.

k_open_a.text: The Assembly wrote a great deal that summer. Here is what it meant to do.

f_1.text: Three barricades between us and the Bastille. Don't walk lines into them, gentlemen. Break them with the guns first.

r_1.text: The mortar throws over a barricade, Marshal. Set it up out of their muskets' reach, five to eleven tiles off.

t_1.text: There are families behind those shutters, Marshal. They did not all choose this.

f_t1.text: Then we end it quickly. That is the mercy I can give them.

v_saved.text: Sir. The Hollins boys, all six of us. We are here for the Father, and for you.

t_saved.text: I baptised your sister's boy, Will. Keep your head down for him.

tip_foundry.text: The Foundry casts more guns and mortars, each with a horse from the Breeder. The treasury pays us every minute.

tip_powder.text: Ten shots a musket, Marshal, then the bayonet. Keep the powder wagon close behind the line: it fills them again.

r_rush.text: They are coming out over the barricade! Canister, load canister!

tip_canister.text: CANISTER on the gun's card: a cone of balls down the street. Keep the line in front of the guns.

f_bar_1.text: The first barricade is ours. Bring the guns up.

f_bar_2.text: Two. The third is the strongest: the Bastille is behind it.

f_2.text: Now the river. They hold the bridges to the Cité.

t_2.text: Marshal, look at the far bank. They are carrying torches towards Notre-Dame.

f_2b.text: Then we take the bridges at the run. Notre-Dame does not burn while I command here.

f_magazine.text: The Bastille's powder magazine is ours. The wagon and the muskets fill up there now, not back at the camp.

n_lyon_sullen.text: Lyon men are on the bridges: weavers who walked from the Croix-Rousse to fight.

n_lyon_risen.text: Half of Lyon's Assembly is on the bridges and at the Bastille, under its own flags.

t_lyon.text: I know some of those faces. From the weavers' square.

n_torch.text: Torch-bearers on the Petit Pont, for the cathedral.

t_nd.text: The doors are burning! Men onto the parvis!

f_bridges.text: Both bridges. The Cité is ours.

f_3.text: Now the Hôtel de Ville. Varenne is in there. I want him alive: the King will judge him, not a musket ball.

r_3.text: They have palisaded the whole square. The guns will open it.

tip_3.text: Take him alive: wear him down, then a man of ours beside him. If he reaches the river, he is gone.

f_breach.text: The palisade is open. Watch the west gate: he will run.

n_flight.text: Varenne is out by the west gate, running for the boats at the Port Saint-Nicolas.

n_quay.text: A boat is waiting at the quay. Its oarsmen are already at the oars.

va_taken.text: You have taken a man, Marshal. You have not taken an idea.

f_taken.text: I have taken the man who burned Virginia. That will do for today.

t_mercy.text: Marshal. I ask for his life. Send him away, but let him live. I prayed for his men in Virginia; I pray for him now.

f_order.text: The King gave me the right to judge him here. The Father asks for mercy. The order is yours.

f_spared.text: Exile, then. A ship, and never French ground again.

va_spared.text: You will regret your mercy, Marshal. Or I will make you glad of it. We shall see.

f_exec.text: The law, then. At dawn, on the Grève.

va_exec.text: Do it in daylight. Let them all see what the Crown is.

t_exec.text: I will stay with him tonight, Marshal. Someone should.

f_won.text: Paris was the King's again by morning. The bells of Notre-Dame rang for Lauds.

r_marshal.text: The Marshal is hit! Keep him behind the line!

f_priest.text: The Father is hurt! Men round the priest!

n_nd_burnt.text: Notre-Dame is burning. The whole city can see it.

n_escaped.text: A boat pushes off from the Port Saint-Nicolas. Varenne is gone down the river.

a_1.text: Hold the barricades. Burn Notre-Dame, bring down the Field Marshal, or get Varenne out by the river: any of them wins Paris.

a_tip.text: Your men behind a barricade are safe from the Crown's line. Not from its guns: when a barricade breaks, rush the guns.

f_end1.text: Paris was quiet by the feast of the Assumption. The barricades went back to being carts and paving stones.

f_end_spared.text: Varenne sailed from Le Havre in September. I did not go to see him off.

f_end_exec.text: Varenne died on the Grève at dawn. The crowd was very quiet.

f_end_saved.text: The Hollins boys went home to Virginia that winter. All six of them.

t_end_spared.text: I said a Mass of thanksgiving in Notre-Dame. The doors were still black with smoke.

t_end_exec.text: I said a Mass for his soul. Some of his men came, and I did not send them away.

k_end_spared.text: Mercy from the victor is still victory. I have never regretted that order.

k_end_exec.text: It was the law. I have read the order a hundred times since. It is still the law.

k_end2.text: That was the end of the Assembly's cities. The next fires were not theirs.

k_end_a1.text: That is not how it went. Paris did not hold.

k_end_a2.text: But if it had, the Crown would have had two capitals, and one of them against it.

new_foundry.text: NEW: THE FOUNDRY. Cast your own Field Cannons now, and the Mortar.

new_mortar.text: NEW: THE MORTAR. It lobs its shell over walls: the barricades are its work, not the line's.

barricade.caption: Paris, July 2769. The barricades of the faubourg.

notre_dame.caption: Torches on the bridges of the Cité.

text: Paris, July 2769. The Free Assembly holds the city: three barricades across the faubourg, the bridges of the Cité, Varenne in the Hôtel de Ville.
Break the barricades with your guns (the Mortar is new: it lobs over walls), save Notre-Dame from the torches and take Varenne alive.
Field Marshal Fairleigh and Father Tomasz must live.
Paris, July 2769. You are the Free Assembly, and the city is yours behind its barricades.
Burn Notre-Dame, bring down the Field Marshal, or get Varenne out by the river.

crown.title: Paris is the King's
crown.text: The barricades are down, Notre-Dame stands and Varenne is taken.

text_if.text: Varenne is spared: exile, by your order.
Varenne is executed, by your order.

assembly.title: Paris holds
assembly.text: The Assembly's flags still fly over the Hôtel de Ville.
